# ADR-007: Reference data generated by a script, committed

Supersedes ADR-005's storage and refresh (D1 + cron). Its principle stays: everything comes from the TfL
API, nothing is typed in by hand.

## Context
Phase 1 measured the inputs: ~84 timetables (2 check stations × 2 directions × 21 lines) at 318–506 KB
each, plus 21 route sequences up to 144 KB. A Worker run has 10 ms CPU and 50 subrequests (D1 included),
so a cron could process ~3 timetables per run: ~30 runs to fill, during which no mismatch can be raised.
Timetables change a few times a year.

## Decision
- `bun run reference` (`scripts/build-reference.ts`) fetches lines, route sequences, timetables and a sample
  of arrivals, derives check stations, normal gaps per hour band, service hours and platform directions,
  and writes `src/shared/reference/rail.json` (compact, deduplicated).
- The file is committed and bundled with the Worker. `generatedAt` is served with every response.
- `src/shared/reference/overrides.ts` corrects automatic choices, each with a reason.

## Alternatives
| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| Cron → D1 (ADR-005) | ~30 runs to fill; empty reference after deploy; CPU risk per run |
| Scheduled GitHub Action → D1 | Needs Cloudflare credentials in CI (rejected: CI holds none) |
| Fetch on request | Latency and subrequests on the hot path |

## Consequences
- No runtime cost or failure mode; reference changes are reviewable diffs in git.
- Staleness is manual: re-run the script when TfL changes timetables or lines. The README says so, and the
  age is visible in `/api/status`.
- A line added by TfL after generation is shown status-only until the file is regenerated.
